title: THE MARRIAGE OF DOCTOR FRANCIS LE BARON AND MARY WILDER (Illustration)
note: Catalogue text: DOCTOR FRANCIS LeBARON. Plymouth was often without a physician. * * * In 1694 there was no surgeon there, and the wife of Goodman Hunter is said to have been in much suffering for want of one. A French privateer had just been wrecked in Buzzard’s Bay ; her accomplished surgeon, only twenty-six years old, was FRANCIS LeBARON, supposed to be the scion of some Huguenot family then in royal disfavor, and bearing an assumed name. While in Plymouth, on his way to Boston as a prisoner-of-war, he heard of Goodwife Hunter’s case and treated it with great success. The selectmen procured his release by Lieutenant-Governor Stoughton, and his settlement at Plymouth as their surgeon. He married Mary Wilder, of Hingham, September, 1695, and died nine years later, at Plymouth, where his quaint little head-stone on Burial Hill is now remarkable for its beautiful finish and preservation.—Goodwin’s Pilgrim Republic, Note, page 380.
